annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Snapshot service for Famulus. Takes read-only btrfs snapshots of managed subvolumes (for example etc and var) before AI-initiated system mutations, records the rpm-ostree deployment digest active at snapshot time, and restores snapshot sets on rollback. One Create call covering multiple subvolumes yields exactly one snapshot_ref, matching the one snapshot_ref field of the C1 audit event that triggered it.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Create read-only btrfs snapshots of each named managed subvolume, as one atomic set. subvolumes is an ordered list of managed btrfs subvolume names (each matching [a-z0-9._-]+); unknown or unmanaged names raise org.famulus.Snapshot1.Error.UnknownSubvolume. tag MUST begin with the lowercase UUIDv7 event_id of the C1 audit event that triggered the snapshot, optionally followed by a dot and a free-form suffix; the UUIDv7 part is embedded in the returned snapshot_ref. The rpm-ostree deployment digest active at snapshot time is recorded in the snapshot metadata. Returns a snapshot_ref of the form famulus-snap/<event_id>/<subvols>@<unix_ts>.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Restore every subvolume in the set identified by snapshot_ref, as an all-or-nothing attempt. Returns true on success; returns false only when the restore was attempted and cleanly rolled back to the pre-restore state. Raises org.famulus.Snapshot1.Error.NotFound for an unknown ref and org.famulus.Snapshot1.Error.Busy if another restore is in flight. A reboot MAY be required for the restore to take full effect.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: List all snapshot sets. Each entry carries at least: snapshot_ref (s), event_id (s), subvolumes (as), tag (s), created_unix (t), deployment_digest (s). The a{sv} dictionary is deliberately open; consumers MUST tolerate unknown extra keys.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Keep the newest keep_last snapshot sets (ordered by created_unix) and delete all older sets. Returns the number of sets pruned. Snapshot sets referenced by C1 audit records are still prunable; the audit log outlives its snapshots.
